review_notes:
I reviewed all four theorems in the file (lines 1–118). I also read the lemmas they call: `exists_remote_scaling_sequence` (RemoteScalingSequence.lean), `exists_remote_scaling_conjugations` and `scaling_vector_limit` (RemoteScalingLimit.lean), `scaling_defect_tendsto_of_cyclic` (ModularDefectDensity.lean), `ModularConjugationData` (including `fixes_vector`) and `rightAction` (ModularRightAction.lean). The proofs of `exists_modular_graph_shift` and `exists_modular_graph_shift_adjoint` are already a single `obtain` plus `exact`, and I found nothing to simplify there.

There are two findings, both in the first two theorems:
1. A `funext`/`rw` detour that only flips the sign of a commutator can be folded into one `simpa`.
2. The derivation of the limit at Ω is copied word for word in two proofs.

I could not run Lean, so neither replacement has been compiled. The `simp only` lemma set in finding 1 is the same one the existing `heq` proof uses. Finding 2 only moves existing proof lines into a helper lemma.

findings.excerpt:
have heq : (fun n => (v n*a-a*v n).val Ω) =
      (fun n => -((a*v n-v n*a).val Ω)) := by
    funext n
    simp only [AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub,sub_apply,neg_sub]
  rw [heq]
  simpa only [neg_zero] using (hcentral a Ω).neg
findings.problem: The proof needs `v n*a - a*v n → 0`. It gets this from `hcentral`, which gives the reversed commutator `a*v n - v n*a → 0`. To do so it states a function equality with `funext`, rewrites the goal with it, and then calls a separate `simpa` to clear `-0`. That is three steps, two of them bookkeeping, for what is just negating a limit.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace lines 50–56 with a single normalization step using the same lemmas:
```lean
  intro a
  simpa only [AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub, sub_apply, neg_sub, neg_zero] using
    (hcentral a Ω).neg
```
(not compiled). `simp only` rewrites `-((a*v n - v n*a).val Ω)` in the hypothesis to `(v n*a).val Ω - (a*v n).val Ω` and `-0` to `0`. The goal normalizes to the same form, which is exactly what the `heq` proof already does.
findings.benefit: The idea, "swap the commutator by negating the known limit", now fits in one line that names the source (`(hcentral a Ω).neg`). The reader no longer has to read a function-level equality and a `rw` whose only job is to reverse a subtraction. Nothing becomes more opaque: the `simp only` set is explicit and is the one the original `heq` proof uses.

have hscale := scaling_vector_limit J S.separating S.cyclic s v hs
    (fun n => (hv n).1) (fun n => (hv n).2.2.1) (fun n => (hv n).2.2.2)
  have he (n : ℕ) : d.rightAction (v n) Ω =

    change d.conjugation (star (v n).val (d.conjugation Ω)) = _

findings.problem: Lines 73–79 repeat lines 37–45 of `exists_modular_scaling_all_vectors` character for character. Both use the same `hscale` call, the same `he` proof (`change` then `rw [d.fixes_vector,hd]`), and the same closing `simpa`. Both upstream lemmas (`exists_remote_scaling_sequence` and `exists_remote_scaling_conjugations`) give the same hypothesis shape `Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 r) ∧ (∀ n, 0 < s n ∧ s n < 1 ∧ v n*star (v n)=1 ∧ StateScales …)`. So this one step, "a scaling sequence with ratio t² has Ω-defect tending to 0 for the modular right action", is proved twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Factor the shared step into one helper placed before both theorems, for example:
```lean
include S in
private theorem modular_scaling_defect_at_vector (J : H ≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℂ] H)
    (d : ModularConjugationData M Ω)
    (hd : d.conjugation = tomitaPolarConjugation J Ω S.separating S.cyclic)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (s : ℕ → ℝ) (v : ℕ → Algebra M)
    (hs : Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 (t^2)))
    (hv : ∀ n, 0 < s n ∧ s n < 1 ∧ v n*star (v n)=1 ∧ StateScales M Ω (s n) (v n).val) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (v n).val Ω-(t : ℂ) • d.rightAction (v n) Ω) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have hscale := scaling_vector_limit J S.separating S.cyclic s v hs
    (fun n => (hv n).1) (fun n => (hv n).2.2.1) (fun n => (hv n).2.2.2)
  have he (n : ℕ) : d.rightAction (v n) Ω =
      tomitaPolarConjugation J Ω S.separating S.cyclic (star (v n).val Ω) := by
    change d.conjugation (star (v n).val (d.conjugation Ω)) = _
    rw [d.fixes_vector,hd]
  simpa only [he,Real.sqrt_sq ht] using hscale
```
Then lines 37–45 become `have hΩ := S.modular_scaling_defect_at_vector J d hd ht.le s v hs hv`. In `exists_modular_coisometry_sequence`, the `?_` at line 72 is filled by the same term, which removes lines 73–79. (Not compiled.)
findings.benefit: Each theorem then shows only what makes it different: which remote sequence it uses, and, in the first theorem, the extension from Ω to all vectors. The shared step (identify the right action at Ω with the Tomita conjugation, then apply `scaling_vector_limit` with √(t²) = t) is stated once under a descriptive name. A reader no longer has to check that two seven-line blocks really are identical.
